context:
Goal: a session can tap the iPhone simulator only while it holds that device, so it never acts on a device another session uses.
Problem (risk): the new guard passed every cloud test, but no one has tried it on a real simulator, where a lane once kept tapping after its hold ended.
Based on (read): the cloud session has no Xcode tools, so it cannot boot a simulator.
Departs from: main lets any session tap a booted simulator — the change refuses a tap from a session that does not hold the device.
Why yours: the test needs the simulator on your Mac, and no Mac folder is shared with any session (checked 2026-11-12 16:05 CST: the computer folder list is empty), so no session can reach it.

options.gain: The guard can merge with its live check done.
options.how: Paste into Claude Code on your Mac: "In the claude-settings checkout, run `git fetch origin sim-tool-lease-check-3` and check out commit f323e46806 in a new worktree, then install its hooks for this session only. 1. Run `sim-test --hold --for 900` through the Monitor tool and wait for its "sim-test: holding <UDID>" line. 2. Tap and screenshot that device with the simulator tool; both must work. 3. End the hold, then tap again; the guard must refuse it with rule simulator-device-lease. 4. Confirm the device shut down, the lease was given back and the lock is free. Reply with one line per step: PASS or FAIL and what you saw." Pick this if every line says PASS.
options.label: All four steps passed
options.lose: About 15 minutes of your Mac's simulator time.

options.gain: The lane fixes the failure before merge.
options.how: Same paste; pick this and put the FAIL lines in the note box.
options.label: A step failed
options.lose: About 15 minutes of your Mac's simulator time.

ref: draft PR #3011 (simulator tool needs the caller's own lease), head f323e46806
title: On your Mac: check that the simulator tool works only while a session holds the device
why: It needs Xcode's simulator, which only your Mac has.
